title: LLM gateway
description: Every team calls models through one gateway that applies budgets, reuses answers, picks a provider and fails over when one is down.

detail.role: Chatbots, batch jobs and agents that need a model.
detail.why: They call one stable API and never hold a provider's key.

detail.role: Authenticates each application, applies its limits and presents one API whichever model is used.
detail.why: A new provider or model becomes a configuration change, not a code change in every app.

security.text: Provider keys exist only here, in a secrets manager. An app leak exposes no provider key.

cost.text: Requests per minute and tokens per day are capped for each application.

detail.role: Returns a stored answer for a repeated or near-identical prompt.
detail.why: A hit costs almost nothing and answers in milliseconds.

cost.text: Typical hit rates of 10 to 30 percent on support-style traffic remove that share of the bill.

risks.text: Caching suits repeatable questions. It is switched off for personalised prompts and for any call that sets a temperature.

detail.role: Chooses a model for each request by task, cost and latency target, and retries on another provider when a call fails.
detail.why: Cheap models handle easy work and the expensive one is kept for what needs it.

cost.text: Short classification and extraction calls go to a small model at a fraction of the price.

risks.text: A rule that sends hard prompts to a weak model lowers quality without raising an error. It is checked against the evaluation set before each change.

detail.role: Tracks running spend against each team's monthly budget and tells the router to allow, downgrade or stop.
detail.why: Overspend is stopped by the system, not found on the invoice.

cost.text: At 80 percent the team is alerted and moved to cheaper models. At 100 percent calls are refused.

risks.badge: Risk: a hard stop is an outage
risks.text: A team that hits its limit mid-incident loses its feature. Critical apps have an override that a named owner can approve.

detail.why: Chosen on quality for the main tasks and on price.

security.text: Traffic stays off the public internet and is not used for training.

risks.text: Providers throttle and fail. This is why a second provider is wired in.

detail.role: Takes over when the primary is slow, throttled or down.
detail.why: A second vendor means one outage does not stop every answer.

cost.text: No reserved capacity, so it costs nothing while idle.

risks.text: Another model answers differently, so prompts are tested against both. Fallback answers are tagged in the logs.

detail.role: Records tokens in and out, model, latency and cost for every call, tagged by team and use case.
detail.why: Spend and quality can be explained by who caused them.

security.text: Only counts and tags are kept by default. Prompt text is logged for sampled calls and redacted.

detail.role: Shows each team its spend, cache hit rate and cost per feature.
detail.why: Teams that can see their spend manage it.

cost.text: A monthly report goes to each team lead, which is usually enough to prompt changes.

links.label: Model request
links.detail: One API shape for every model. The response streams back on the same connection.

links.label: Cache lookup
links.detail: Before spending anything, the gateway asks whether this prompt was answered recently.

links.label: On a miss
links.detail: A request with no cached answer goes to the router with its team and task tags.

links.label: Within budget?
links.detail: The router asks whether the team may spend, and whether to downgrade to a cheaper model.

links.label: Primary call
links.detail: The normal path, with a timeout of a few seconds before giving up.

links.label: Failover
links.detail: Used when the primary times out, is throttled or returns a server error. The same request is resent unchanged.

links.label: Usage record
links.detail: Every call, including failed ones, writes one record after it ends.

links.label: Aggregates
links.detail: Hourly totals feed the dashboards and the budget alerts.
